messages:
Luke (Support): heads-up — were getting a cluster of customer tickets (e.g. #9873, #9876) reporting 502/504 for hosted inference since ~09:13 after the morning canary. Error spike coincides with the canary ramp. Anyone oncall?

deploy-bot: canary/deploy succeeded at 2024-06-18T09:12:08Z — config toggle 'fast_prefetch' = true applied to canary group (10% traffic).

Priya (Oncall): on it. Can someone paste an example request + trace-id and a quick curl repro? Also link to the dashboard (errors / latency).

Luke (Support): sample curl from customer ticket:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer XXX" \
  -H "X-Trace-Id: tr-0a1b2c3d" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Body: {"error":"upstream_error","message":"gateway timeout"} 
Trace: tr-0a1b2c3d

Jon (Eng): looking at gateway logs now. I see a high rate of 502/504 with logs like:
```
proxy.go:423 upstream reset: HTTP/1.1 502, err="connection reset by peer"
router.go:112 header rewrite dropped 'Authorization' (len before=8192, after=4096)
```
Some canary hosts show auth header truncation on large requests. That would cause auth failures upstream and 5xx.

Sasha (SRE): graph: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/5xx-spike shows spike at 09:13 across us-east-region frontends. CPU/ram look fine; error is concentrated on nodes in the canary subset. I recommend an immediate rollback of the canary traffic to stable while we triage.

Maya (PM): customer impact? Which customers/tiers affected? Any billing/elevated-SLA hits yet? We should notify CS and keep them updated.

Priya (Oncall): Jon, please roll back the canary traffic. Preserve the canary instances for debugging (do not terminate). Command to shift traffic back to stable: 
```
# run in infra-admin
redwoodctl rollout traffic set --service inference-api --to stable --from canary --reason "5xx spike after canary flag" --preserve-canary
```
I'll create an incident channel and loop in CS.

Jon (Eng): starting rollback now. Running:
```
$ redwoodctl rollout traffic set --service inference-api --to stable --from canary --reason "5xx spike"
Initiating traffic reweight: canary 10% -> 0%
Applying change... OK
```
deploy-bot: rollout change accepted (id r-20240618-0918). Traffic reweighted to stable.

Sasha (SRE): metrics update: error rate dropping — 5xx now falling toward baseline after traffic shift. p50/p95 latencies stabilizing. Will watch for 10m.

Luke (Support): opening proactive CS messages to affected customers and linking this incident. Billing note: no suspicious unit spikes, looks like requests failed before heavy token usage, but flag for finance to watch for retries.

Jon (Eng): preliminary root cause (dev notes): the 'fast_prefetch' toggle had a selector mis-specified so a header-rewrite path got enabled on canary hosts only. That code path truncates long headers (bug in header-merge). For requests with large Authorization headers (some customers send signed JWTs), upstream treats truncated auth as invalid -> gateway retries -> 5xx. Next steps: patch header-merge to preserve auth header, add unit test for long headers, and make canary selector stricter.

Maya (PM): good rollback. Schedule postmortem tomorrow 11:00. Tagging: sev2, customers impacted (list in incident doc). Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
